question-limit/spec-only-haiku/3.note: Gap suite only. Allowances are keyed on `${contributor}\u0000${task}`, so contributor "a\u0000b" on task "c" shares an allowance with contributor "a" on task "b\u0000c". The spec says allowances are separate per task and per contributor and does not restrict id characters. Marginal: only ids containing NUL collide; the 15 other separators in the same test pass.

reverse-diff/spec-only-haiku/3.note: Gap suite only. The test's first hunk header declares 7 old / 8 new lines but is followed by one line, then two more `@@` headers. The submission tracks hunk line counts, so it treats those later headers as hunk body and leaves `Sheet` after the second `@@` unmapped. The spec does not say whether a hunk's declared counts are trusted or `@@` headers are recognised by pattern alone; the reference does the latter. Not in the writer's open list, so a suite defect, not a spec-tightening item.

patch-apply/double-blind-own-haiku/18.note: The parser ends a hunk at any line starting "--- " or "+++ " before the header counts are met, so a removed line whose text is "-- old" is read as the next file header and the hunk is refused as short. The spec defines a hunk by its counts and only calls a hunk with fewer lines malformed; within the counts a line is a hunk line whatever it starts with. Unlike reverse-diff/spec-only-haiku/3, the test agrees with the counts. Marginal.

coalescing-cache/spec-only-haiku/5.note: Gap suite. A stale read starts a background refresh; when the entry expires before that refresh settles, a get returns the expired value instead of waiting for the in-flight load. The spec says an expired value is never returned from then on and one load runs at a time per key.

patch-apply/double-blind-rule-haiku/17.note: Passed both suites; caught by the git oracle (bin/git-oracle). applyPatch skips any section without --- and +++ headers (`if (oldPath === undefined || newPath === undefined) continue;`), so git's form of a rename with no hunks, which has neither header, leaves the file at its old path. The spec says a rename with no hunks moves the text unchanged. The public suite writes every pure rename with both headers; the blind hidden suite had git's form, the gap suite does not, and this run was never graded by the blind suite.
